sections.h2: Is gloss just shinier, or does it actually change the print?
sections.html:
It changes the print. A gloss surface is smooth at a microscopic level, so light bounces straight back instead of scattering. The effect on ink is the same as wetting a pebble: colors look darker and more saturated, blacks look deeper, and a photo looks like a photo rather than a copy of one. That is why bright brand colors, gradients and anything photographic are printed glossy by default.

Matte is the sibling finish, and the honest comparison is this. Gloss gives you color depth and an easy-wipe surface, and in return shows glare under spotlights and fingerprints on dark areas. Matte gives up some punch for readability and a softer look. If your sticker is mostly text or will be photographed under studio lights, our custom matte sticker page explains when to switch. For a logo with a saturated red or a full-color illustration, stay here.

sections.h2: Gloss vinyl, gloss BOPP or gloss paper: what the base changes
sections.html:
Gloss is a surface treatment, so the material underneath sets the durability. Gloss vinyl is the all-rounder: waterproof, flexible, 3 to 5 years outdoors with a laminate, and the right base for cars, coolers, water bottles and outdoor signs. Gloss BOPP is a thinner film that resists oil and water and costs less than vinyl, which makes it the label stock for sauces, soaps and cosmetics. Gloss paper is the cheapest, looks bright on a box or an envelope, and must stay dry.

Lamination is the one extra worth paying for on vinyl that goes outside or gets handled. The coating alone gives the shine; the laminate adds a second clear film that stops scratches and slows UV fade. For indoor labels and giveaway stickers, the coating is plenty and keeps the unit price down.

sections.h2: Where a glossy finish is the wrong call
sections.html:
We sell a lot of gloss, so it is worth being straight about the jobs it does not suit. Switch to matte, or ask us about it, if any of these describe your sticker.

  • Labels under retail spotlights or on glass shelves, where the hot spot of reflection lands on the name.
  • Stickers that need to be written on: gloss sheds ballpoint and most markers.
  • Black or navy backgrounds that will be handled, where fingerprints stand out.
  • Product photos shot with flash, where the flare has to be retouched out.
  • Tiny text under 6 point on a busy background, which can shimmer and blur.

The middle path is spot UV: a matte base with gloss applied only to the logo or a key shape. You keep the readability of matte and get the shine where it earns its place. Holographic is the other way to add shine without gloss; our custom holographic sticker range gets its sparkle from the film rather than the coating.

sections.h2: Applying glossy stickers so the shine stays even
sections.html:
A gloss surface shows every bubble and crease as a bright ripple, so application matters more than it does on matte. These steps give a flat, even finish on bottles, laptops and bumpers alike.

  1. Clean the surface with isopropyl alcohol and let it dry. Skip household glass cleaner; the residue stops the adhesive bonding.
  2. Peel the liner away from the sticker rather than the sticker away from the liner, so the edge never gets a fingernail crease.
  3. Stick down one edge, then roll the sticker on with a credit card, pushing air ahead of it.
  4. Press the whole face firmly for a few seconds. Full adhesion takes about 24 hours.
  5. On curved bottles, warm the sticker with your hands first so it wraps without wrinkles.

For gloss vinyl on vehicles, apply above 50 degrees Fahrenheit and out of direct sun, and leave it a day before the first car wash.

sections.h2: Getting a gloss sticker run quoted and printed
sections.html:
Send the artwork as PDF, AI, EPS or SVG, or as a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at the finished size, along with the quantity, the shape and the surface it is going on. The surface tells us whether to quote vinyl, BOPP or paper. A digital proof lands in your inbox within a business day, design help is free, and nothing prints until you approve it.

Minimum is 100 per design. Production takes 5 to 7 business days from approval, and FedEx delivery anywhere in the United States is included. Rush is available on request at the quote stage. Glossy stickers can share a shipment with any other finish or material from the Die Cut Stickers home page, which is the easy way to compare gloss and matte from the same file in one order.

faqs.a: On vinyl or BOPP, yes. The gloss coating sheds water and the film underneath does not absorb it, so bottles, coolers and car bumpers are fine. Gloss paper stickers have a shiny surface but a paper core that wrinkles when wet, so keep those on dry packaging.

faqs.q: Do glossy stickers fade in sunlight?
faqs.a: Unlaminated gloss vinyl holds up for a year or two outdoors before the colors soften. Add a gloss laminate and the sticker lasts 3 to 5 years in sun and rain. Indoors, fade is not a concern at all with either option.

faqs.q: Why do my colors look brighter on a glossy sticker than on screen?
faqs.a: The smooth gloss surface reflects light straight back, which makes inks look more saturated than the same print on matte or the same colors on a backlit screen. We match to Pantone references on request if an exact shade matters more than the extra punch.

faqs.q: Can glossy stickers be die cut to a custom shape?
faqs.a: Yes. Any outline, from a simple rounded rectangle to a character silhouette, cut with a thin border so the edge never clips the art. Gloss laminate goes on before cutting, so the shine runs right to the edge of the shape.

faqs.q: Will a glossy sticker leave residue when I peel it off?
faqs.a: With removable adhesive, no, for roughly a year after application. Permanent adhesive may leave a trace on some plastics, which isopropyl alcohol removes. The gloss surface itself has nothing to do with residue; that is all the adhesive choice.

faqs.q: Can I order glossy labels for food jars and sauce bottles?
faqs.a: Yes. Gloss BOPP is the standard food label stock: thin, oil and water resistant, and happy in the fridge. We print full color with Pantone matching and supply on rolls or sheets. The inks are standard print inks, so the label sits on the outside of the container, not in contact with food.

faqs.q: Is gloss or matte better for a bumper sticker?
faqs.a: Gloss, for most designs. Colors read brighter at distance and the smooth surface sheds road grime in the car wash. Choose laminated gloss vinyl at 3 x 11.5 inches with rounded corners, which resist lifting at highway speed far better than square ones.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest glossy sticker option for giveaways?
faqs.a: Gloss paper or unlaminated gloss vinyl in a 2 to 3 inch size, kiss cut on sheets. Pricing starts at $0.30 per sticker and drops as the count rises from the 100-piece minimum. Sheets are quicker to hand out at events than loose pieces.

faqs.q: Can glossy stickers be written on with a marker?
faqs.a: Not reliably. Ballpoint skates off and most markers smear on a gloss coating. If you need a writable area for dates or names, ask for a matte finish, or a matte base with spot UV gloss on the logo only, which gives shine where it counts and a pen-friendly area elsewhere.

faqs.q: Do glossy decals work on car windows?
faqs.a: Yes. Laminated gloss vinyl goes on the outside of the glass, or we can print a face-adhesive version to apply from inside. Outside is brighter; inside lasts longer because the weather and the wiper never touch it. Both come off cleanly with heat and a plastic scraper.

faqs.q: How many glossy stickers can I order at once?
faqs.a: From 100 to tens of thousands per design. Under about 1,000 we print digitally; larger runs move to offset for a lower unit price. Production stays at 5 to 7 business days after proof approval unless you request rush, and FedEx shipping in the US is free at any count.

faqs.q: What file type gives the sharpest glossy print?
faqs.a: Vector: PDF, AI, EPS or SVG. Edges stay crisp at any size and the gloss coating makes a blurry raster edge more noticeable, not less. If you only have a PNG or JPG, export it at 300 dpi at the finished size and we will check it on the proof.
